purpose: Bounded Malaysia Act 872 route from statutory remedy architecture to a reported first GrabCar Tribunal hearing, while preserving merits, correction, payment, durability, trust, and exit as open.

events.geography: Malaysia; national Gig Workers Act 2025 route
events.date_precision: day; Ministry implementation notice states enforcement began on this date
events.denominator: One national statutory implementation route; the Ministry's stated covered-worker count is not an independently audited case denominator
events.method: Structured extraction from Malaysia Ministry of Human Resources Act 872 implementation materials
events.missingness: Worker awareness, platform compliance, complaint use, case volume, correction, payment, and later worker outcomes are not retained
events.exposure: Act 872 brought statutory rights concerning automated monitoring and decisions, non-automated review, written reasons, hearing, and dispute routes into force
events.alternatives_before_action: Workers and platforms could use internal complaint, conciliation, Tribunal, association, or other legal routes; actual choice among them is not observed
events.immediate_burden_or_benefit: The route makes formal information, review, explanation, and dispute rights available while adding procedural and evidentiary requirements
events.choice_or_response: The Ministry reports enforcement and publishes implementation, complaint, conciliation, and Tribunal materials
events.person_or_actor_with_control: The Ministry and statutory bodies control implementation and procedure; platforms and workers control later participation within the legal route
events.remedy_or_institutional_response: A statutory platform-worker remedy architecture is reported in force
events.immediate_outcome: The comparative route advances from proposed or prospective design to a national legal framework in force
events.protected_outcome: Workers receive a formal route to information, review, explanation, hearing, and dispute resolution on paper
events.sacrificed_outcome: Compliance, comprehension, time, evidence, and access burdens may remain with workers and platforms; their distribution is not measured
events.cost_risk_transfer: The framework shifts some review and dispute obligations to platforms and public institutions while leaving case participation and evidence access unresolved
events.later_outcome: Actual use, compliance, correction, payment, restored access, durable work, trust, and exit remain open
events.meaning_and_attribution: The law frames platform control as a subject of worker rights; worker interpretation and legitimacy are not measured
events.public_or_collective_response: Formal consultation and institutional routes are visible; later worker collective action is not joined
events.counterexample: A remedy architecture can be legally in force without showing that a worker can use it or obtain a practical correction
events.source_and_uncertainty: Official Malaysian Ministry of Human Resources implementation materials and Act 872; legal availability is not evidence of exercised or effective remedy

events.geography: Malaysia; Gig Workers Tribunal and Gig Consultation Council
events.date_precision: day; Ministry announcement reports formal establishment and appointments
events.denominator: One national Tribunal and consultation-council establishment event
events.method: Structured extraction from official Ministry appointment and implementation announcement
events.missingness: Caseload, worker use, case identifiers, hearing quality, decision reasoning, award, payment, and enforcement are not retained
events.exposure: The statutory remedy route acquired named institutional bodies and subsidiary procedural rules
events.alternatives_before_action: A worker could remain outside the route, use internal or conciliation processes, seek association or family assistance, or pursue another remedy; no case-level alternative is observed
events.immediate_burden_or_benefit: A formal Tribunal can lower the distance between a dispute and human adjudication, while preparation, evidence, language, time, and representation burdens remain unknown
events.choice_or_response: The Ministry reports appointment and establishment of the Tribunal and Council and publishes procedural materials
events.person_or_actor_with_control: The Tribunal and Ministry control institutional procedure; workers and platforms control whether and how they present a dispute
events.remedy_or_institutional_response: The state-level dispute-resolution infrastructure is reported as established
events.immediate_outcome: The legal right is attached to a visible institutional route rather than only statutory text
events.protected_outcome: Potential access to conciliation, hearing, and award procedures becomes more concrete
events.sacrificed_outcome: The public record does not show whether the institution has sufficient capacity, independence, evidence access, or worker support
events.cost_risk_transfer: The institution may absorb adjudication work while participants bear filing, preparation, attendance, and proof burdens
events.later_outcome: Actual filings, merits review, correction, payment, restored platform access, recurrence, trust, and exit remain open
events.meaning_and_attribution: Institutional establishment may shape perceived reachability, but no worker belief or trust measure is available
events.public_or_collective_response: A public institutional route is announced; participant or collective response is not measured
events.counterexample: A named Tribunal can exist and still have no publicly visible award or worker-level outcome for a reported case
events.source_and_uncertainty: Official Malaysian Ministry announcement and Tribunal materials; establishment is not evidence of caseload or effectiveness

events.geography: Kuching, Sarawak, Malaysia; one reported GrabCar Tribunal proceeding
events.date_precision: day; hearing date reported by two public reports
events.denominator: One named reported Tribunal proceeding; no public primary case identifier or worker sample
events.method: Structured extraction from two public reports attributing the first-hearing facts to the Malaysian Ministry/Tribunal route
events.missingness: Filed claim, case number, legal provision, evidence, hearing record, merits reasoning, award, payment, account correction, later work, trust, and exit are not retained
events.exposure: A GrabCar worker's dispute over platform operation, Saver Trips, cashback incentives, and Advance Booking reportedly reached a Tribunal hearing
events.alternatives_before_action: The public reading of Act 872 describes an internal complaint and conciliation route before Tribunal referral, with a deactivation exception; the claimant's route, association support, other work, or non-use is not observed
events.immediate_burden_or_benefit: A hearing makes human procedural review visible, while eligibility, route sequencing, representation limits, evidence burden, time, income loss, and technical access remain unknown
events.choice_or_response: The claimant reportedly appeared personally, GrabCar used an employee representative, and the matter returned for evidence and additional witness examination
events.person_or_actor_with_control: The Tribunal controls hearing procedure; the claimant and GrabCar control their submissions and representation within the reported route
events.remedy_or_institutional_response: A concrete platform dispute reached the formal hearing and evidence stage
events.immediate_outcome: Institutional use is reported beyond legal design or company commitment
events.protected_outcome: The claimant obtained a reported opportunity to present the dispute to a formal Tribunal
events.sacrificed_outcome: The public record does not show whether the hearing protected income, access, dignity, or future work
events.cost_risk_transfer: Personal appearance may lower legal-representation cost while leaving evidence, technical knowledge, time, and organizational capacity unequal
events.later_outcome: Decision, correction, payment, restored access, durable work, trust, recurrence, and exit remain open
events.meaning_and_attribution: The hearing may affect perceived institutional reachability, but no worker meaning or trust outcome is measured
events.public_or_collective_response: A reported case has entered a public institutional stage; wider worker response is not observed
events.counterexample: A first hearing and pending evidence stage can occur without a public award, payment, correction, or worker recovery
events.source_and_uncertainty: Human Resources Online and Free Malaysia Today reports, the official Act 872 text, and a secondary access-route reading checked 2026-09-20; primary case file, award, and outcome were not located in the checked packet

arrows.evidence: Official Ministry implementation materials report enforcement and institutional establishment
arrows.counterexample: Legal and institutional availability does not establish worker access, use, or effectiveness
arrows.remaining_gap: Worker awareness, platform compliance, caseload, evidence access, and exercised remedy

arrows.to: reported GrabCar dispute reaches a hearing
arrows.evidence: Two public reports describe a first GrabCar Tribunal hearing in Kuching on 1 September 2026
arrows.counterexample: A reported hearing may reflect one exceptional case and does not estimate route accessibility or volume
arrows.remaining_gap: Primary case identifier, filing route, denominator, worker effort, and generalizability

arrows.evidence: The public reports state that the matter returned for evidence and additional witness examination
arrows.counterexample: Procedural continuation is not a merits finding or effective human review
arrows.remaining_gap: Hearing record, evidence, legal reasoning, next date, and decision

arrows.to: correction, payment, or restored platform access
arrows.evidence: No public award, payment, access correction, or enforcement outcome was located in the checked packet
arrows.counterexample: A case can be heard and remain unresolved, dismissed, settled privately, or produce no practical correction
arrows.remaining_gap: Primary case file, award or settlement, payment, access change, and enforcement

arrows.to: durable work, trust, recurrence prevention, or exit
arrows.evidence: The public record contains no worker-level follow-up after the reported hearing
arrows.counterexample: Even a favorable award can fail to restore usable work, income, trust, or durable security
arrows.remaining_gap: Worker receipt, later platform status, earnings, recurrence, trust, continued work, switching, and exit

boundary: This ledger records a comparative statutory and reported procedural route. It does not establish a violation, effective human review, platform compliance, award, payment, correction, worker recovery, trust, or exit.
storage_boundary: Only compact public legal and procedural observations are retained; no worker identity, claim file, platform data, or restricted Tribunal record is added.
